summary: CI/tooling change, router and agent unchanged: implements TM-16's next action 'Refresh the Python locks regularly' as a check (ADR-0144, proposed). Reviewed against the previous trusted versions of tools/security/lock_requirements.py and .github/workflows/security.yml (flagged for explicit maintainer review). lock_requirements.py: cmd_resolve's pip invocation moved unchanged into pip_resolve (same flags: --dry-run, --only-binary=:all: so no sdist build code runs, CPython 3.11, manylinux x86_64; only the Linux refusal text is reworded); resolve's output is byte-for-byte the same path. New read-only command outdated: pip_resolve of CI_REQS, compares router, container and CI lock entries by canonical name, released() reads the first upload time from PyPI's JSON API (urllib, 30 s timeout, failures surface as before in pypi()), fails only for versions older than --grace-days (default 30, negative refused before any network). It writes no file. security.yml: new job python-lock-freshness only on schedule and workflow_dispatch (never push or pull_request, so PR code never runs in it and upstream releases cannot block PRs), workflow-level permissions contents: read, actions pinned to the same SHAs (check_pinned_references: 0 findings), installs nothing. No existing check, audit, trigger or condition removed; selftest_dependency_audit still passes. AGENTS.md gains one sentence on the weekly run. The risk register drops the done v0.35.1 provenance action (run 45630953077, 2026-11-25).

tests.evidence: 7 tests (1 skipped on Linux by design): nothing pending when pip picks the locked versions (canonical names); newer release overdue only past the grace (30 days exactly not), router lock compared too, unknown date listed not overdue, longer grace keeps it pending; dropped/added CI packages listed never overdue; the command passes on the current locks, fails for an overdue release and names the explicit bound, passes inside the grace; a negative grace is refused before pip runs (rejected case); non-Linux refused; the workflow job runs only on schedule/dispatch with the default grace. Without the change: 7 errors.

tests.command: python tools/security/lock_requirements.py outdated (WSL Ubuntu, Python 3.14 venv, live PyPI)
tests.evidence: 0 pending changes with the default grace and with --grace-days 0; instrument probe: pip resolved 31 packages, all equal to the CI lock; a lowered aiohttp entry (3.9.0) was reported as 'aiohttp 3.9.0 -> 3.14.5 (released 45 days ago, OVERDUE)'.

tests.command: every python test/... and tools/... command of all workflows in .github/workflows/ (Windows), plus ruff check ., router.py --check --pure, check_pinned_references, selftest_dependency_audit
tests.evidence: 104 commands, 1 failed: the new 'lock_requirements.py outdated' step itself, which refuses Windows by design ('pip resolution runs on Linux only'); it passed in WSL (above).

limitations: The scheduled job itself has not run on GitHub yet; its first run is the next weekly schedule or a manual dispatch.
Entries only the router or container lock has (not needed for the CI target) are not compared.
A PyPI outage turns the weekly run red, as for verify-pypi.
The end-to-end suite was not run: no router or agent code changed.
